messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T09:02Z started: rev=release/2026-03-15-09 (sha abc123). Canary to 10%

incident-bot: Alert: service:redwood-inference p99 latency > 3s for 5m (threshold 1.2s) — paging anna (oncall)

anna (oncall): seeing p95 ~800ms, p99 hitting 4-7s and a spike in 502/504 + downstream reset errors. marking incident. paging sam and eng-sre.

sam (runtime): thanks. rolling logs now. quick hypothesis: new kernel path in runtime picks a different socket keepalive/backpressure path. possible connection pool starvation to model-backend.

lee (observability): graph: https://grafana.redwood/overview?panel=latency&p99 shows big step at 09:03Z coincident with canary. queued_requests metric up x6. kv_cache hit rate unchanged. network retransmits increased.

mike (support): getting customer reports of slow responses and some 503s from the hosted API; estimated impacted requests ~1.8% of traffic but high-profile customers hitting retries.

priya (product): can we toggle fallback to previous stable model variant for the canary? want to reduce customer-visible errors ASAP.

kira (eng-ops): we can route canary traffic to stable pool by flipping routing policy for release tag. preparing command.

sam (runtime): quick debug: enabling per-connection metrics: seeing many connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT on canary hosts and long GC pauses on worker process. suspect new kernel path interacts badly with epoll batching under our nginx->runtime multiplexing.

anna (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) divert canary traffic to stable revision (route change) 2) enable circuit-breaker on canary instances to short-circuit slow backends 3) if no improvement in 5m -> rollback. executing 1 now.

kira (eng-ops): run: 
```
rcctl route set --service redwood-inference --selector release=release/2026-03-15-09 --weight=0
rcctl route set --service redwood-inference --selector release=stable --weight=100
```

infra-bot: Route change applied. Canary weight -> 0, Stable -> 100.

lee (observability): within 60s p95 dropped to 400ms, p99 trending down to 1.2s, errors reduced by ~70%. queued_requests down.

sam (runtime): enabling CB on canary instances (for safety) even though traffic removed. command: 
```
rbctl config update --service-runtime canary --circuit-breaker 0.5s
```

infra-bot: Circuit breaker config applied to canary pool.

anna (oncall): still seeing residual 5xx from older canary hosts but low volume. recommend rolling rollback to be safe (full rollback of release/2026-03-15-09).

priya (product): agreed — customers care more about reliability than this feature. proceed with rollback and then postmortem. notify support.

kira (eng-ops): initiating rollback: 
```
deploy-bot rollback --service redwood-inference --target stable --reason "p99 latency regression after canary"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started. Rolling canary instances to stable rev. Estimated 3m.

anna (oncall): monitoring during rollback. pinging support for customer-facing note. @mike please prepare message for affected customers (SLA note + mitigation).

mike (support): drafting: "We observed elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors affecting a subset of requests after a canary deploy. We rolled back the release and service latency has returned to normal. If you continue to see issues, please reply and include request IDs." will send out once rollback completes.

lee (observability): post-rollback metrics show p99 back to baseline ~450ms, error-rate back to normal. no sustained increase in downstream error budget.

sam (runtime): root cause notes (preliminary): new runtime kernel path changes batch flushing and keepalive handling, which under certain multiplexed connection load causes worker threads to stall and sockets to accumulate in CLOSE_WAIT, exhausting ephemeral fds and causing upstream proxies to return 502/504. reproducible under high connection churn and long-tail requests.

anna (oncall): immediate mitigations we did: 1) diverted traffic off canary 2) applied circuit-breaker config 3) rolled back release. Good catch everyone. Moving to severity: sev2 -> closing active paging.

priya (product): schedule a postmortem and block re-release until runtime fix + e2e canary test that simulates connection churn.

sam (runtime): I'll open an RFC and patch branch with keepalive fixes and additional socket exhaustion guards. will add a canary test that floods short-lived connections.

oliver (oncall-next): taking handoff at 09:15Z. any outstanding actions for next oncall?

anna (oncall): handoff notes: monitor p95/p99 for 30m, watch queued_requests and CLOSE_WAIT sockets on hosts with tag release/2026-03-15-09, ensure rollback completed and no re-deploys for this release. If any regressions, escalate to sam and kira.

oliver (oncall-next): acked.

priya (product): I'll coordinate customer comms and add follow-up to roadmap.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: incident_id=INC-2026-0315-07, duration=13m, impact=partial (errors/timeouts ~1.8% traffic; notable customers affected). Postmortem required.

mike (support): customer message sent to affected customers.

sam (runtime): quick log snippet from canary host showing socket pileup: 
```
[09:03:12] socketfd=10234 state=CLOSE_WAIT age=243s backlog=512
[09:03:13] worker-12 blocked for 1.8s at epoll_wait
[09:03:14] upstream reset: ECONNRESET
```

anna (oncall): adding this thread to the incident board and assigning to sam/kira for RCA. closing channel notifications. :white_check_mark:

kira (eng-ops): created task INFRA-3241 "runtime keepalive & socket exhaustion guard" and scheduled canary test.

sam (runtime): thanks, will follow up with PR and test plan.

priya (product): thanks team — closing out.

deploy-bot: Note: release/2026-03-15-09 remains blocked from re-deploy until rc:approval from runtime+eng-ops.

anna (oncall): last check @09:18Z — metrics stable, incident closed.
